plain: To add at the end of what has been said

webster.text: To add at the end; to add after something else has been said or written; as, to subjoin an argument or reason.

example.quote: MARTIN moved to subjoin to the last amendment the words "in the recess of the Legislature"
example.cite: James Madison, Notes of Debates in the Federal Convention of 1787, August 30, 1787
